---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source("../r/style.R")
source("../r/course.R")
```

The group project is assessed with the rubric below. The same rubric is used for feedback on the interim report
in W6 and on the defence in W8, so you know at every point what is expected. Assessment and participation
conditions for a particular run of the course are announced by the course team before the course starts.

## Criteria and weights

| Criterion | Weight | Observable anchor for a strong project |
|---|---:|---|
| Question, data unit and comparison | 15% | Purpose, time zero, population and baseline fit the decision. |
| R analysis, validation and uncertainty | 25% | Someone outside the group can reproduce a figure and identify the independent test data set. |
| Ethical weighing and communication | 15% | One affected person, one conflict of goals and the reasoned consequence are concrete. |
| Regulatory classification | 10% | Intended purpose, role, relevant source and open classification are traceable. |
| Data protection | 10% | Data flow, legal or review question, recipients and deletion point are consistent. |
| Information security | 10% | A plausible threat receives an effective control, a test and a responsible role. |
| Recommendation, defence and revision | 15% | The recommendation states conditions, a named counter-position and a verifiable next step. |

: Assessment criteria of the group project. The weights add up to 100%. {#tbl-rubric-weights}

## Levels

Every criterion is scored on the same four levels.

| Level | Meaning | Example for "data protection" |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | **Missing.** The criterion is not addressed. | No data flow. |
| 1 | **Named.** The relevant point is mentioned in general terms. | "Patient data are pseudonymised." |
| 2 | **Evidenced in the case.** The point is worked out for this project with its specific facts. | A data flow with recipients, purpose and a deletion point for the gait videos. |
| 3 | **Evidenced, tested against an alternative and translated into the decision.** | As level 2, plus a comparison with keeping only joint angles, and the recommendation to delete raw videos after 30 days. |

: The four levels of the rubric. {#tbl-rubric-levels}

## Scoring rule

$$
\text{project percentage} = \sum_{k=1}^{7} \text{weight}_k \times \frac{\text{level}_k}{3}
$$

For runs with a grade, the course proposes 60% for the individual examination and 40% for the group project:

$$
\text{course percentage} = 0.6 \times \text{examination percentage} + 0.4 \times \text{project percentage}
$$

The split is a proposal; the course team states the conditions that apply before the course starts. Self-assessment
and peer feedback serve as feedback only and never enter a grade.

## Worked example (fictitious)

A fictitious group receives the following levels. The calculation is done in R so that every step can be checked.

```{r}
#| label: rubric-example
rubric <- data.frame(
  criterion = c("Question, data unit and comparison", "R analysis, validation and uncertainty",
                "Ethical weighing and communication", "Regulatory classification", "Data protection",
                "Information security", "Recommendation, defence and revision"),
  weight = c(15, 25, 15, 10, 10, 10, 15),   # percent
  level  = c(2, 3, 2, 1, 2, 2, 3)           # fictitious levels 0-3
)
rubric$points <- rubric$weight * rubric$level / 3
project_percent <- sum(rubric$points)

exam_correct <- 15                           # fictitious: 15 of 20 questions correct
exam_percent <- 100 * exam_correct / 20
course_percent <- 0.6 * exam_percent + 0.4 * project_percent

rubric
c(project = project_percent, examination = exam_percent, course = course_percent)

# Checks: the weights add up to 100 and the example is reproduced exactly
stopifnot(sum(rubric$weight) == 100, all(rubric$level %in% 0:3),
          isTRUE(all.equal(project_percent, 230 / 3)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(course_percent, 0.6 * 75 + 0.4 * 230 / 3)))
```

The fictitious group reaches `r cdsr_number(project_percent, 1)`% in the project. With 15 of 20 examination questions
correct (`r cdsr_number(exam_percent, 0)`%), the proposed weighting gives `r cdsr_number(course_percent, 1)`% for the
course. Use the example to calibrate assessors: two assessors score the same project independently, compare their
levels criterion by criterion and agree on the reasons before scoring further projects.

## Common mistakes the rubric catches

- An AUC without the number of independent test units (criterion 2 stays at level 1).
- "Data are anonymised" without a data flow (data protection stays at level 1).
- A control without a test ("we use encryption") stays at level 1 for information security.
- A recommendation without a condition for stopping is at most level 2.
